projects.title: CyberLabs Microservices Fleet
projects.subtitle: Modular NestJS Architecture & Multi-Node Administration
projects.tagline: Orchestration of cyberlabs-admin, core backend APIs, and vm-service nodes with role-isolated permissions and MongoDB Atlas cluster management.

highlightRepos.name: cyberlabs-admin
highlightRepos.description: Zero-Trust administrative console with custom NestJS RBAC guards.

highlightRepos.name: cyberlabs-backend
highlightRepos.description: Core transactional microservice API communicating over private VPC networking.

highlightRepos.name: cyberlabs-vm-service
highlightRepos.description: Compute node provisioning daemon managing DigitalOcean droplet lifecycles.

projects.overview: CyberLabs operates as a decoupled microservices architecture designed to isolate administrative operations from public endpoints. The platform partitions workloads across three primary services: cyberlabs-admin for privileged cluster control, backend for transactional business logic, and vm-service for provisioning cloud compute nodes.
projects.problem: As infrastructure instances and administration complexity grew, running a monolithic codebase caused deployment coupling, risk of unauthorized access across administrative actions, and high database write contention.

architectureDetails.frontend: Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, customized accessible dashboard panels.
architectureDetails.backend: NestJS microservices communicating via secure internal HTTP/gRPC interfaces, with JWT role-based guards and metadata reflection.
architectureDetails.infrastructure: DigitalOcean Droplets in a VPC private network, Cloudflare Zero-Trust edge access and SSL termination.
architectureDetails.data: MongoDB Atlas multi-region replica set with dedicated indexes and connection pooling via Mongoose.

engineeringDecisions.decision: Service Separation between cyberlabs-admin and vm-service
engineeringDecisions.rationale: Ensured compute-heavy VM provisioning scripts cannot degrade response latency for mission-critical administrative control panels.
engineeringDecisions.tradeoff: Introduced inter-service RPC communication overhead, mitigated by keep-alive HTTP agents on private VPC networks.

engineeringDecisions.decision: Custom Decorator & ExecutionContext Guard in NestJS
engineeringDecisions.rationale: Enforced compile-time role assignment (@Roles('SYSADMIN', 'OPERATOR')) with runtime validation against JWT claims before hitting business controllers.
engineeringDecisions.tradeoff: Required strict JWT payload versioning to avoid stale permissions after user tier demotions.

engineeringDecisions.decision: Index Strategy & Read Preferences on MongoDB Atlas
engineeringDecisions.rationale: Used secondary-preferred read preferences for read-heavy system telemetry queries while confining writes to the primary replica.
engineeringDecisions.tradeoff: Accepting brief eventual consistency (typically <100ms) on non-critical dashboard telemetry.

codeArtifact.description: Production NestJS execution context guard validating role bitmasks and JWT identity.

projects.title: Eduko Learning Platform
projects.subtitle: Next.js App Router Architecture & Automated Delivery
projects.tagline: Frontend engineering migration to Next.js App Router with Server Actions, tag-based cache revalidation, and automated CI/CD via GitHub Actions and Vercel.

highlightRepos.name: ahmedhabiby/Eduko1
highlightRepos.description: Core Next.js platform repository delivering the modern educational interface.

projects.overview: Eduko is an educational platform serving dynamic course material, interactive assessments, and high-concurrency learner traffic. Ahmed co-developed the frontend layer, transitioning complex UI state into Next.js App Router paradigms with React 19.
projects.problem: Legacy client-side data fetching caused sluggish initial page loads, layout shifts during course catalog rendering, and cumbersome manual deployments that delayed feature releases.

architectureDetails.frontend: Next.js 15/16 App Router, React 19 Server Components, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion.
architectureDetails.backend: Node.js REST API with Redis caching layer.
architectureDetails.infrastructure: Vercel Global Edge Network with automated staging branch previews.
architectureDetails.data: PostgreSQL database accessed via optimized API endpoints and cached at edge.

engineeringDecisions.rationale: Rendered course catalog and syllabus content on the server, eliminating client waterfall fetch requests and reducing JavaScript bundle size by over 40%.
engineeringDecisions.tradeoff: Required strict isolation between interactive client components ('use client') and server data-fetching modules.

engineeringDecisions.rationale: Used Next.js revalidateTag('course-[id]') inside Server Actions upon course updates, keeping content static at the edge until an instructor edits it.
engineeringDecisions.tradeoff: Requires deliberate tag naming conventions across all mutations to prevent cache leaks.

engineeringDecisions.decision: Automated Pull Request Previews via GitHub Actions
engineeringDecisions.rationale: Every pull request triggered automated linting, type checks, and a live preview URL on Vercel, preventing regressions before merging into main.
engineeringDecisions.tradeoff: Added roughly 90 seconds to PR checks, heavily offset by catching syntax and styling defects early.

codeArtifact.filename: course-actions.ts (Next.js Server Action with Cache Invalidation)
codeArtifact.description: Type-safe Next.js Server Action with Zod input validation and on-demand cache revalidation.

screens.title: Course Catalog & Edge Shell
screens.description: Server-rendered lesson directory with zero cumulative layout shift and atomic cache tagging.

screens.title: Interactive Assessment Engine
screens.description: Real-time state validation, optimistic quiz submission, and automated score compiling.

screens.title: GitHub Actions Automated Pipeline
screens.description: Automated linting, bundle size analysis, and zero-downtime edge previews on every PR.
